cards.text: Jesus has been in Bethany, where they hosted a dinner for Him (John 12:2). The next day, the great crowd in town for the feast hears that Jesus is coming to Jerusalem. Friend, that news moves faster than a group chat after somebody texts “Big news. Call me.”

cards.question: With palm branches in hand, the great crowd goes out to ___ Jesus.

cards.text: Out they go, and they are LOUD. “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”

cards.question: The crowd going out to meet Jesus also shouts that He is the King of Israel.

cards.text: Then Jesus finds a young donkey and sits on it. Me, I never ride anything, friend, because this gold base goes everywhere with me, so I just HOP.

cards.question: The Gospel of John says Jesus sat on that young donkey just as something said He would. What?

cards.text: Then the Gospel of John quotes the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 9:9), with words for the Daughter of Zion: “See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.”

cards.question: Those written words speak to the Daughter of Zion about her King coming on a donkey's colt. What do they tell her?
Jesus' disciples understand these things about the young donkey and the written words right away.

cards.text: It's after Jesus is glorified that His disciples remember what was done to Him and realize these very things were written about Him. Friend, that's me finally getting a joke three days after somebody told it, laughing alone in the bakery at nothing.
Meanwhile, there are many people around who were with Jesus the day He called Lazarus, His friend from Bethany (John 11:1, 11), from the tomb and raised him from the dead.

cards.question: The people who were there when Jesus raised Lazarus keep quiet about what they saw.
The Gospel of John gives another reason the crowd went out to meet Jesus. What is it?

answers.text: They heard He would be crowned
They heard He was giving gifts

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of Jewish religious leaders, huddle up and talk it over with one another.

cards.question: Watching the crowd, the Pharisees tell one another that things are going well for them.

cards.text: They tell one another it's doing them no good: “Look how the whole world has gone after Him!” Friend, that's two coworkers whispering by the copier, “Well, THIS isn't working,” while the entire office lines up behind somebody else.
